content.text:
I read the actual implementation before answering — the diagnosis matters more than generic advice here.

## What's actually wrong

Four separate things compound in that screenshot, and only one of them is a layout problem.

**1. Every edge carries an always-on label.** `entity-type-graph-view.tsx:458-461` sets `label` unconditionally. Member→Company has three *different* relationship types, so three labels land at nearly the same midpoint, plus the Member self-loop's label on top. Text on edges is the thing that scales worst — collisions grow with edge count and no router solves label placement well.

**2. Parallel edges aren't bundled.** `entity-schema-graph.ts:158` keys the collapse on `${rt.slug}|${source}|${target}`, so it only folds *sibling rules of the same relationship type*. Three distinct types between the same pair still draw three paths.

**3. Node width is a hard 220px** (`entity-schema-graph.ts:91`) and the header packs icon + name + "18 fields" + count into one flex row (`:121-144`). The name is `truncate` and `flex-1`, so it's the only thing that yields — metadata wins space over identity. That's backwards, and it's why you get `Comp…`.

**4. ELK's routing is computed and then thrown away.** `ELK_OPTIONS` sets `edgeRouting: ORTHOGONAL` plus four edge-spacing options (`:324-340`), but `layoutSchemaGraph` only reads `laidOut.children` (`:387`) — never `laidOut.edges[].sections`. React Flow then re-routes with `smoothstep` between evenly-spaced handles. You're paying for lane reservation and discarding it.

## What best-in-class actually does

The comparables are Azimutt, ChartDB, drawDB, Supabase's schema visualizer, and Neo4j Bloom. The consistent pattern across all of them:

**ERDs don't put text on edges.** Relationship identity lives at the endpoint (marker/badge), on hover, or in a side panel. Never floating at a path midpoint. Your relationships are semantic (`works_at`, `claims_identity`) rather than FK-derived, so you genuinely need the name — but you need it *on demand*, not always.

**One drawn line per node pair.** Multi-edges collapse to a single path with a count chip, expanding on hover/selection.

**Progressive disclosure beats better layout.** Azimutt's default view is deliberately *not* the whole schema — it seeds from an entry point and you expand outward. Past ~25 types no layout tuning saves you, and that's the honest answer to "no matter how many edges."

## The concrete fix, in impact order

**Tier 1 — fixes your screenshot outright**

Bundle every ordered pair into one edge regardless of relationship type: change the pair key to `${source}|${target}` and carry a `relationships[]` array instead of a single label. Member→Company becomes one line with a `3` chip. Then make labels conditional: render `label` only when the edge is in focus — the connected node is hovered or selected, or a cluster is focused. Also drop the label when the drawn path is shorter than the text. Default canvas is bare lines + arrowheads; hover a node and its edges light up with names.

**Tier 2 — fixes `Comp…`**

Go two-line: name at full node width on line 1, `18 fields · 2,035` muted on line 2. Height 44 → ~56. Then measure the label and size per node — `width = clamp(180, textWidth + chrome, 320)`. ELK already accepts per-node widths, they just all pass 220 today. Long names then get room instead of being clipped, and the metadata stops competing.

**Tier 3 — makes it hold at 50 types**

Give ELK explicit ports with `elk.portConstraints: FIXED_ORDER` (one port per edge, in handle order), read back `laidOut.edges[].sections[].bendPoints`, and render a custom edge that draws that exact polyline. Parallel edges then get real, separately-assigned lanes. Bonus: pass `labels: [{width, height}]` per edge and ELK does label placement for you, so focused labels never collide either.

**Tier 4 — the real scale answer**

Open on the largest cluster rather than the full graph. You already built the cluster panel and the focus mechanism — flip the default from "everything drawn, others dimmed" to "biggest cluster drawn, rest listed in the panel and expandable." That's the only thing that's genuinely bounded as the workspace grows.

---

Tiers 1 and 2 together would clean up exactly what you screenshotted, and they're contained changes to `entity-schema-graph.ts` and the edge/node memos in `entity-type-graph-view.tsx`. Tier 3 is the structural one and touches the ELK boundary plus a new custom edge component.

**Confidence: high (85)** on the diagnosis — I read the layout module, the graph builder, and the view, and each claim above maps to a specific line I verified (the discarded `laidOut.edges` at `entity-schema-graph.ts:387`, the per-relationship-type pair key at `:158`, the unconditional label at `entity-type-graph-view.tsx:458`). I have not booted the page, so I haven't confirmed how these render at other schema sizes.

**Next actions you can pick from:**
- Have me implement Tier 1 + 2 in a worktree, with before/after screenshots from the booted app against your real `buremba` schema.
- Prototype Tier 3 (ELK ports + bend-point consumption) alone first, since it's the change that decides whether Tier 1's bundling is even needed long-term.
- Tell me roughly how many entity types a large workspace has — if it's over ~30, Tier 4 should jump the queue ahead of Tier 3.
- Decide the hover-vs-click interaction for revealing bundled relationship names; hover is smoother but click is what makes it usable on touch.

The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.

**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].

**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.

**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
```
cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
```
`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.

**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
```
/api/auth-config       -> 200
/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
```
See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).

**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
```
cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
```

**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. Skipping the handshake returns `Bad Request: Server not initialized`.

Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)

# Session token from the DB (prod DB serves both targets)
DB="$(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)"
TOKEN=$(psql "$DB" -tAc "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Drive the browser

```bash
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify eval "document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=$SIGNED; path=/; secure; samesite=lax'"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify open "https://app.lobu.ai/<path>"
agent-browser --session lobu-verify wait --text "<expected text>" --timeout 25000
agent-browser --session lobu-verify snapshot -i      # find @refs
agent-browser --session lobu-verify click @e13        # interact
agent-browser --session lobu-verify screenshot --full /tmp/out.png
agent-browser --session lobu-verify close
```

name: project_lobu_ai_prod_db
description: Prod DB cluster is now lobu-ai-prod-db (replaced summaries-db) after the 2026-05-20 test-against-prod wipe + PITR recovery
metadata:

---

On 2026-05-20 the `summaries-prod` production `owletto` database (49 orgs / 36 users / ~1.17M events, ~12GB) was **wiped**: a developer ran the integration test suite locally with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at prod; `__tests__/setup/test-db.ts` setup runs `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` and the `summaries` role owns the DB, so it succeeded (ran ~16:59–17:27 UTC). NOT CI (CI uses throwaway `lobu_test`).

**Recovery:** CNPG PITR from R2 backup lineage `summaries-db-v2` to 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC (latest verified-complete snapshot) into a NEW cluster **`lobu-ai-prod-db`** (clean name chosen by user). The old `summaries-db` was retired/deleted.

**Current prod topology (CNPG on k8s, ns `summaries-prod`):**
- DB cluster `lobu-ai-prod-db` + pooler `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` + daily ScheduledBackup; backups to R2 serverName `lobu-ai-prod-db`.
- GitOps-managed at `packages/owletto/deploy/k8s/apps/lobu-db/` via its OWN Flux Kustomization `lobu-db` (separate path so it escapes the lobu app overlay's `summaries-` namePrefix → keeps the clean name). The lobu app overlay (`apps/lobu/overlays/summaries-prod`) no longer defines a DB; app+migrate `poolerService` point at `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` / `lobu-ai-prod-db-rw`.
- App DB creds secret `summaries-db-app` (NOT cluster-owned — survives cluster deletion). R2 creds `summaries-r2-backup-credentials` (SealedSecret).

**Prevention shipped (lobu#989, merged `df38fbf4`):** `getTestDb()` refuses any DB whose name isn't test-shaped (`assertSafeTestDatabaseUrl`; override `LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1`); baseline `00000000000000_baseline.sql` `migrate:down` is now `RAISE EXCEPTION` (was `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`). owletto #208 (cutover) + #209 (GitOps codify) merged.

**Querying prod (verified 2026-07-30).** The database is named **`owletto`** — not `lobu`, not `app`. `app` exists and is empty of app tables, so a wrong `-d` fails with a confusing `relation "runs" does not exist` rather than a missing-database error. The primary pod has two containers, so `-c postgres` is required:

```
kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
  psql -U postgres -d owletto -A -F$'\t' -c "<sql>"
```

Column names that do not exist and cost a retry each: `runs.updated_at` / `runs.approved_at` (the real ones are `created_at, completed_at, claimed_at, last_heartbeat_at, run_at, expires_at`), `entities.merged_into_id` (it is `merged_into`), `entity_identities.kind` (it is `namespace`). There is no `notifications` table.

**PITR recovery runbook lessons (do these BEFORE cutover next time):** (1) PITR resets planner statistics → run `ANALYZE` or queries seq-scan and time out (`resolve_path` hit this). (2) A hand-made recovery cluster has NONE of the chart's tuning/resources — copy `shared_buffers`/`random_page_cost=1.1`/`effective_cache_size`/resources from the chart. (3) `geo_earthdistance` migration needs `cube`+`earthdistance` extensions pre-created as superuser (app role can't CREATE untrusted earthdistance) and conflicts with pre-squash `geo_lookup(p_lat,…)` (`DROP FUNCTION` it first). (4) CNPG `bootstrap` is immutable — a GitOps manifest adopting an existing recovered cluster MUST replicate its exact bootstrap or the webhook rejects the apply. (5) Flux `prune: true` on the apps Kustomization — removing a cluster from render deletes it; verify `kustomize build` before merge.

content.text:
Done and verified against prod data. Vite is still running on **http://localhost:5174/buremba/memory** if you want to poke at it yourself (it's proxying to `app.lobu.ai`, and your existing localhost session cookie should carry over).

## What changed

**Edge bundling** (`entity-schema-graph.ts`) — the pair key went from `relationshipType|source|target` to `source|target`, so all relationships between two types share one path and carry a `relationships[]` array. Your schema went from **6 drawn paths to 3**.

**Labels on demand** (`entity-type-graph-view.tsx`) — replaced the built-in `smoothstep` edge with a `SchemaEdge` component. At rest a path shows only a count chip, and only when it bundles more than one relationship. Hovering a node or an edge reveals the names, stacked and truncating at 180px with the full text in a tooltip. That bounds visible labels by one node's degree instead of by graph size.

**Two-line nodes** — name on line 1 owning the full width, `18 fields · 2,035 records` on line 2. Width is now computed per node from whichever line is longer, clamped 200–320px. The meta string is composed in the graph module because the width is measured from it — two builders would let measurement drift from rendering.

**Default framing** — this one was beyond the two tiers I described, but the fix wasn't complete without it. Your workspace has 11 unconnected types stacked in a column taller than the canvas, so `fitView` was framing the island list and pushing Member/Company/Person off the top edge. `fitViewOptions.nodes` now frames only the connected subgraph. The islands are still on the canvas and still in the side panel.

## Evidence

Resting canvas, read from the DOM: `edges: 3`, `labels: ["3", "2"]` — the only text is the two count chips. Hovering Member returns `["Claims Identity\nHas Authority\nProposes Merge With", "Claims Identity\nProposes Merge With"]` — all five names, none colliding. `Comp…` now renders as `Company`.

Gates: 96 tests pass across `src/components/entities` (33 in the graph module, 10 in the view), `tsc --noEmit` clean, biome clean on all four files.

## Confidence

**High (88) on the rendering and bundling** — verified in a real browser against prod data, both at rest and on hover, reading the DOM rather than eyeballing a screenshot.

**Medium (65) on the node-widening path** — every type name in your workspace is short enough to land on the 200px minimum, so all boxes came back the same width. The widening and the 320px clamp are covered by unit tests only; I never saw a long name render. The char-width constants are estimates, so a long name may truncate a little earlier than the box could actually hold.

**Not attempted:** Tier 3 (consuming ELK's bend points instead of re-routing in React Flow) and Tier 4 (progressive disclosure for large schemas). Neither was needed to fix what you screenshotted.

## Next actions

- Create a type with a deliberately long name (or point me at an org that has one) so I can verify the widening and clamp in the browser rather than just in tests.
- Decide on touch: hover is the only way to reveal names right now, and click is taken by navigation. A tap-to-reveal mode would need the click behavior rethought.
- Ship it — I'd run `make pre-pr`, `make review-fix`, then open the PR with the before/after comparison page. Say the word and I'll take it through.
- Revisit Tier 3 if you expect schemas past ~25 types; bundling bought a lot of headroom but ELK's reserved lanes are still being discarded.

On 2026-07-27 I proposed folding Models into a merged Connect surface because `AgentProviderCatalogItem` has the same fields as `ConnectorDefinitionItem`. The user pushed back and was right: a model provider is *what thinks*, a connector is *what you reach*, a sandbox/device is *where it runs*. Similar fields, different questions.

**The test:** can you describe the grouping out loud without a conjunction? "Connect to / thinks / runs" passes. "Connectors, models, sandboxes and devices" is a list, not a category.

**Also: separate the GOAL from one implementation of it.** The real win was "an operator can see everything broken in one place." I assumed that required merging the pages, and designed the expensive version. A cross-cutting attention view across three tabs delivers the same win without flattening anything. Ask what the goal needs before assuming it needs the big change.

**Landing shape for Lobu (2026-07-27):** three tabs — Connectors, Models, Runtime (= sandboxes + devices, both answer "where does my agent execute"). Plus one attention view spanning all three. Device-provided connectors (Screen Time, Photos) must ALSO appear under Connectors with their device named — a device is two things, a runtime you install and a source of connectors, and a clean three-way split otherwise hides them from anyone searching for what their agent can read.

Related: [[project_connect_surface_merge]], [[feedback_check_prior_sessions_before_designing]], [[feedback_structural_not_usage_deletion_evidence]]

content.text:
I've got the full picture. The two surfaces are very different sizes, which changes the answer for each:

- **New relationship** — a Dialog with 6 short controls (type picker, name, symmetric toggle, source, target). Small, and genuinely canvas-contextual: you're picking two boxes that are visible on the map, which a dialog currently covers. Moving it to the panel is a clear win, and it retires a Dialog that's already off-policy (your no-sheets rule reserves dialogs for OAuth + the command palette).
- **Create entity type** — `EntityTypePage` → `EntityTypeForm`, 9 field groups including a metadata-schema editor, a backing SQL query, and measure columns. It already renders *inline on the same `/memory` route* at `max-w-3xl`, replacing the graph — not a separate page or a dialog. Squeezing that into a 240px column would be a downgrade.

So I'd move one and not the other, which is different from what you asked for — worth checking before I build.

content.text:
Yes — good call on the primary button, that's in. Here's where it landed.

## The split I made

I moved **New relationship** into the panel but left **Create entity type** as a toolbar action, because the two aren't the same size:

- The relationship form is 5 controls, and its two main inputs are *From* and *To* — which are boxes on the canvas. The modal was covering the very thing you were picking. Beside the map, the endpoints stay visible and the new edge appears in place the moment you save.
- The entity-type editor is `EntityTypeForm` — 9 field groups including a metadata schema editor, a backing SQL query, and measure columns. It already renders inline on the same `/memory` route (not a separate page, not a dialog). At 276px those controls would be worse than they are today.

I asked about this first but you were away, so I took the reversible option. If you'd rather have a **quick-create in the panel** — name + icon only, drops the box on the canvas, with "Fields and schema" opening the full editor for the rest — that's a clean addition on top and I can do it next.

## What changed

`new-relationship-dialog.tsx` → `new-relationship-form.tsx`, Dialog chrome stripped, `onOpenChange` replaced by `onDone`. The save/retry logic is byte-identical. From/To are stacked rather than the dialog's two columns — at panel width, side-by-side selects truncated the type names being chosen.

`SchemaClusterIndex`/`SchemaClusterPanel`/`SchemaClusterMenu` → `SchemaPanelContent`/`SchemaPanel`/`SchemaPanelMenu`. The panel now leads with a collapsed "New relationship" button, then Clusters, then No relationships. Width 240px → 288px so the selects fit. Authoring is gated on `canAuthor` inside the panel, not on the trigger being hidden.

The narrow-viewport popover trigger went from "Clusters" to "Schema" — a button labelled "Clusters" that contains "New relationship" misleads.

"Create entity type" is now primary.

## Verified in the browser

Clicking "New relationship" in the panel: `dialogs: 0`, aside labels `["Relationship", "From", "To"]`, aside width 276px, canvas fully visible throughout. 97 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean, biome clean.

One cleanup worth flagging: a `biome check --write` I ran over the whole `entities/` directory reformatted four files I never touched (`entity-merge-interaction.ts` and its test, `entity-table-view.tsx`, `entity-type-list-panel.tsx` — ~1300 lines of pure formatter churn). I reverted all four and re-ran the gates green. The diff is now exactly the 6 intended files.

## Confidence

**High (85) on the panel form rendering and gating** — exercised in a real browser, and the admin gate is covered by a test asserting no form controls reach the DOM for a member.

**Medium (60) on the save path** — I did not submit the form. It writes a real relationship into your prod workspace, which isn't mine to do unasked. The mutation logic is unchanged from the dialog and its create-then-retry test still passes, but "click Add relationship against prod and watch the edge appear" is genuinely unrun.

**Low-confidence area: the narrow (<lg) popover.** I renamed the trigger and put the form inside it, but only checked it in jsdom — never at an actual narrow viewport.

## Next actions

- Tell me whether you want the quick-create-in-panel version for entity types after all; it's maybe 40 lines on top of what's here.
- Let me submit the relationship form once against a throwaway pair so the write path is actually proven end-to-end — say the word and I'll create one and delete it.
- Check the <lg> popover at a real narrow width, since that path is only jsdom-verified.
- Ship it: `make pre-pr`, `make review-fix`, then the PR with the before/after page. This is now two concerns on one branch (graph legibility + panel authoring) — I'd split them into two PRs unless you'd rather land it as one.

content.text:
Both are done and verified against prod. Here's the state of each.

## Entity type editor now lives in the panel

You were right to overrule me — it works. Create and edit both open in the panel, the canvas stays live beside them, and the URL never changes.

- The node's pencil no longer links to `/$owner/entity-types/$slug`; it opens that type's editor in the panel. The callback reaches the node via React context rather than node `data`, because `data` is value-compared to decide when a box redraws and a callback has no business in that comparison.
- "Create entity type" opens the same editor in create mode instead of taking over the pane.
- The panel grows 288px → 440px while an editor is open and hands the space back on close. All 7 field groups fit, including the SQL editor and schema builder.
- `EntityTypePage` is reused verbatim — it already owns create, edit, History and the delete zone. I added one `compact` prop: create mode centered its heading, which is right under a full-width tab bar and wrong in a narrow panel.

The routed `/$owner/entity-types/$slug` page stays — the entity-type rail links straight to it, so it isn't dead.

## Needs setup chip removed

Separate branch (`feat/connectors-drop-needs-setup-chip`), since it's a different page. Confirmed: the filter row is one line now, and needs-setup connectors still sort to the top with their row badges — exactly the redundancy you pointed at.

I removed `needs_setup` from the `ConnectorFilter` type, its label, and the matcher too, since nothing else could reach it.

## Two corrections

When I reported the relationship form earlier I said "aside width 276px" as evidence. That was measuring the app's left nav — `querySelector('aside')` matched the first aside on the page, not mine. The form was in the panel, which the labels confirmed, but the number was wrong. Measured properly, the panel is 288px at rest and 440px with an editor open.

I also briefly edited `entity-type-graph-view.tsx` in the *connectors* worktree — a `cd` in a compound command left my shell there. Caught it on the next command and reverted; that worktree now has exactly its three intended files.

## Gates

104 tests pass across `entities` + `settings` (14 in the graph view, including three new ones pinning pencil→panel, create→panel, and no-pencil-for-members). `tsc --noEmit` clean on both worktrees. Biome clean.

## Confidence

**High (85) on create and edit opening in the panel** — both driven in a real browser against prod, reading the DOM: panel at 440px, canvas still mounted, URL unchanged, Company's editor showing History and a locked slug.

**Medium (55) on save.** I never submitted either form. Creating or editing a type writes to your real workspace, and the edit target was `Company` with 2,035 records — not something to poke unasked. The mutation code is untouched, but the full round-trip is unrun.

**Low on layout under stress** — the schema builder's three-column field row and the SQL editor render at 440px, but I only saw an empty create form. A type with 18 fields (Company) in the schema builder at that width is unverified.

## Next actions

- Let me create a throwaway type end-to-end so save is actually proven, then delete it.
- Open Company's editor and scroll the schema builder — 18 fields in a 440px column is the layout risk I can't rule out.
- Decide whether 440px is right, or whether the panel should be drag-resizable.
- Ship: two PRs, one per branch. The connectors one is 3 files and ready now; the memory one is bigger and owes before/after screenshots.

content.text:
Fixed and verified. Answering both questions:

## Mobile — you were right, it was broken

The panel is `hidden lg:flex`, so below `lg` the button set a mode that nothing rendered. My earlier test falsely passed because my viewport command silently failed (`emulate` isn't the syntax — it's `set viewport`), so I was still testing at desktop width.

The fix: below `lg`, an open editor takes the panel full-width and the canvas yields the screen. There's no room for both at 390px, so the editor gets it — the same trade the old routed page made, minus the navigation. The `<lg` popover explicitly refuses to host the editor (`hostsTypeEditor={false}`); it's a `max-w-72` overlay and this is a nine-group form.

Verified at 390×844: name input 358px wide, canvas wrapper `display:none`, Cancel restores both the canvas and the Schema popover. Re-checked at 1440px that the side-by-side path still works — panel 440px, canvas live.

## Expandable — I'd say no, and I have a measurement

I tested the worst realistic case: Company's editor, 18 fields, at 440px. `scrollWidth` 439 vs `clientWidth` 439 — **no horizontal overflow**. The schema builder's three-column field row, the SQL editor, and the icon/color pair all fit. It's dense, but nothing is clipped or unreachable.

Against building it: there's no resizable primitive in the repo and `react-resizable-panels` isn't a dependency, so this means a new dep or a hand-rolled drag handle plus localStorage persistence plus min/max clamping — and the handle sits exactly where React Flow wants pan gestures. That's real cost for a problem the measurement says doesn't exist yet.

The panel already adapts where it matters: 288px for the index, 440px for an editor, full-width on mobile. That's mode-driven sizing, which beats making you drag a divider to get a good result.

If it does start to bite, the cheap version is a single expand toggle in the editor header (440 ↔ ~720px, persisted) rather than free-form drag — no new dep, no gesture conflict. I'd wait for a schema that actually hurts.

## One process note

Twice now a `biome check --write` over a directory reformatted files I never touched — most recently `entity-type-page.tsx`, where it rewrote all 338 lines because that file is in the older 2-space/single-quote style. I reverted and hand-applied my 16 lines in the file's existing style. The remaining biome failures in `entities/` and `entity-types/` are all pre-existing in files outside my diff.

## Gates

104 tests pass (14 in the graph view), `tsc --noEmit` clean, and every file in my diff is biome-clean. Diff is 7 files.

## Confidence

**High (85)** on mobile create/edit and the desktop side-by-side — both driven at real viewports with DOM measurements, not screenshots.

**High (80)** on the 440px sizing verdict — that's a direct overflow measurement on your largest type, not an eyeball.

**Medium (55) on save**, unchanged. I still have not submitted either form; that writes to your real workspace and the edit target was Company with 2,035 records.

## Next actions

- Let me prove save end-to-end with a throwaway type, then delete it — this is the last real gap.
- Ship the connectors branch now; it's 3 files, verified, and independent.
- Decide how to split the memory branch: it's three concerns (graph legibility, panel authoring, type editor in panel) and I'd land it as two or three PRs.
- Revisit the expand toggle only if a real schema turns out to hurt at 440px.

content.text:
Both changes are now on one branch and verified live against the prod backend. `make review-fix` is running in the background (it edits the working tree, so I'm not touching files until it lands).

**On one PR vs. several** — you're right, and I was overthinking it. `AGENTS.md` says one branch = one concern, and the concern here is one thing: making the Memory schema page usable. Legibility, panel authoring, the editor, and the redundant filter chip are all that. I folded the connectors change in (it was 3 files in a separate worktree, now reverted there) and verified it on this branch: the "Needs setup" chip is gone, the other 8 filters intact.

**The drag handle is built.** It's a `role="separator"` between canvas and panel that doubles as the divider — a hairline at rest, accented while grabbed.

Verified live at 1440px against `app.lobu.ai`:

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Drag left 150px | panel 288 → 438, canvas 799 → 649 |
| Reload | restores 438 from localStorage |
| Drag far past the window edge | clamps at 720; canvas keeps 367 (floor is 320) |
| Double-click | resets to 288, clears the stored override |
| Open type editor | 440 default, `scrollWidth === clientWidth` (no overflow) |
| Drag to 600, then close editor | holds 600 — a drag wins over the mode default |
| 390px mobile | handle `display:none`, panel full-bleed 358px, no horizontal overflow |

That last row matters: the 600px override does **not** leak below `lg`, because the width rides a CSS variable behind a `lg:` prefix rather than an inline style.

It's hand-rolled — no new dependency. `react-resizable-panels` would bring a layout engine to a problem that is `startWidth - dx` clamped. Keyboard works too (arrows nudge 16px, Home resets), since the panel hosts the type editor and a pointer-only divider would put that behind a mouse.

**Correcting something I told you earlier:** I recommended holding off on drag-resize because Company's editor showed no overflow at 440px. That measurement was right, but it only answered "does 440 clip content" — not "does the user want a different split." Those are different questions and you were asking the second one.

**Tests:** 36 in the two touched files, 1114 across the suite, all green. I mutation-tested the new ones — flipped the drag direction, dropped the primary-button guard, made the drag lose to the mode default, removed the canvas floor, unhid the handle on mobile. All five were caught.

One thing worth flagging: the full suite failed 12 tests on the first run. Those were 20–30s timeouts in unrelated route tests, caused by two leftover dev servers eating CPU. Killed them, re-ran: 1114 passed in 21s vs 92s. Not related to this change, but I'd have reported a false failure if I'd stopped at the first run.

Next, once review-fix lands: verify its diff, commit by explicit path, and open the PR with the before/after screenshot page the UI-PR rule requires. The save path is still unproven — I haven't submitted any of these forms, since they write to your real workspace.

feat(owletto): make the schema map legible and author from its panel

The Memory schema map was unreadable past a handful of types: relationship
labels collided on the canvas, long type names truncated to "Comp…", and the
island column crowded the schema out of the viewport.

Legibility
- Bundle every relationship between the same pair onto one path (6 paths -> 3
  on the reference workspace). Names leave the resting canvas entirely; a path
  carrying more than one shows a count pill instead.
- Disclose names on hover, on tap (edges are selectable), and via aria-label,
  so the disclosure is not mouse-only.
- Size each box from its measured title and meta text, clamped 200-320px, and
  give the name its own line so identity stops losing space to metadata.
- Frame fitView on the connected subgraph so islands cannot push the schema
  off screen.

Authoring in the panel
- The relationship form and the entity-type editor now render beside the
  canvas instead of in a modal or on a separate route. Both act on the map,
  and both used to hide it -- the relationship form covers the very endpoints
  you pick between.
- The panel widens for the editor and hands the space back on close. Below
  `lg` the editor takes the screen, since there is no room for both.
- Drag the divider to retune the split; the width persists and is clamped so
  the canvas keeps a 320px floor. Double-click or Home restores the default.

Also drops the "Needs setup" filter chip from Connectors: the list already
sorts needs-setup first and badges each card, so the chip only restated what
was on screen.
EOF

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Now building the before/after comparison page for the PR.

**Design plan** — utilitarian, subject is a schema diagram tool:
- **Color**: ink `#15191E`, paper `#FCFCFB`, muted `#6C7580`, rule `#DCE1E6`, accent blueprint-blue `#2E6E8E`, before-marker rust `#A8552E`
- **Type**: system sans for prose, `ui-monospace` for measurements and class names — the page is full of pixel values, so tabular figures throughout
- **Layout**: stacked before/after pairs at full width (the defect is only visible at size), each with a finding strip; a measurements table below

gh pr create --repo lobu-ai/owletto --base main --head feat/schema-graph-legibility --title "feat(owletto): make the schema map legible and author from its panel" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

The Memory schema map (`/$owner/memory`) was unreadable past a handful of types. Three separate defects, all visible in one screenshot: relationship labels collided into each other, long type names truncated to `Comp…`, and the unconnected-types column pushed the actual schema into a corner.

**Before / after screenshots + measurements:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/28ab10d9-2359-41e1-805d-c3b5f39d562e

## Legibility

- **Bundle by pair, not by relationship type.** Every relationship between the same two types now shares one path — 6 paths become 3 on the reference workspace. A bundled path shows a count pill.
- **Names leave the resting canvas.** They are disclosed on hover, on tap (edges are selectable and focusable), and through `aria-label`, so the disclosure is not mouse-only.
- **Boxes size themselves** from measured title and meta text, clamped 200–320px, with the name on its own line. It had shared a row with the counts and was the only flexible item on it, so identity was always what lost space to metadata.
- **`fitView` frames the connected subgraph**, so islands cannot push the schema off screen.

## Authoring moved into the panel

The relationship form was a modal that covered the very boxes you pick between — its two inputs are From and To. Editing a type navigated away to `/$owner/entity-types/$slug`, hiding the map being edited. Both now render beside the canvas.

`EntityTypePage` is reused verbatim rather than reimplemented narrow; it gains a `compact` prop for the heading. The routed page stays — the entity-type rail still links to it.

## Resizable divider

The panel picks a width by mode (288 index / 440 editor), and the divider between canvas and panel drags to override that. Persisted, clamped so the canvas keeps a 320px floor, `Home`/double-click to reset. Hand-rolled: `react-resizable-panels` would bring a layout engine to a problem that is `startWidth - dx` clamped.

## Bug fixed

Below `lg` the panel was `hidden lg:flex`, so **"Create entity type" set a mode that nothing rendered** and the button looked dead on a phone.

- **Red:** at 390px, clicking Create entity type produced no editor; panel computed `display: none`.
- **Green:** panel `flex w-full`, name input 358px, canvas `offsetParent === null`, Cancel restores the canvas. Regression test: `keeps the divider off a narrow viewport, where there is no split`.

The empty state (zero types) still routes to the create page rather than the panel — with no map to keep visible, the panel's whole reason does not apply, and there is no panel rendered to receive the mode.

## Also

Drops the `Needs setup` filter chip from Connectors. The list already sorts needs-setup first and badges each card, so the chip restated what was on screen. Eight filters remain.

## Testing

- `bunx vitest run` — **1128 passed**, 128 files.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `make pre-pr` clean.
- New tests mutation-tested: flipped the drag direction, dropped the primary-button guard, made the drag lose to the mode default, removed the canvas floor, unhid the handle below `lg`. All five caught.
- Verified in a browser against the **production backend** (frontend-only vite proxying `app.lobu.ai`), before shots from an unmodified `origin/main` checkout running alongside.

## Not verified

**The save path.** No create/edit/relationship form in this PR was submitted — that writes to the real workspace, and the edit target was `Company` with 2,035 records. The forms' save logic is byte-identical to what it replaced; what is unproven is that it still works from its new host.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

---
name: reference-owletto-vitest-projects-and-localstorage
description: owletto vitest splits node/jsdom by file extension, and jsdom 29 has NO localStorage — persistence tests need a Storage stub
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`packages/owletto/vitest.workspace.ts` routes by extension, not by content:
`src/**/*.test.ts` → the `node` project (no `window`), `src/**/*.test.tsx` → the
`jsdom` project. A `.test.ts` that touches `window` fails with
`ReferenceError: window is not defined`. Override per file with a
`// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock — it works and does switch the
environment, even though the runner still labels the file `|node|`.

**jsdom 29 has no `localStorage` at all** — it delegates Web Storage to Node's
implementation, which stays inert unless the runner is started with
`--localstorage-file`. Verified in both projects: `typeof window.localStorage`
is `undefined` on a proper `http://localhost:3000` origin.

This matters because `src/lib/storage.ts` (`getStored`/`setStored`) wraps
everything in try/catch and returns `null` on failure. So a persistence test
does not fail loudly — it **passes vacuously** against a null read, or asserts
nothing at all. Install a Storage stub with `Object.defineProperty(window,
"localStorage", {...})` and restore it in `afterAll`.

**How to apply:** any test asserting on persisted UI state (panel widths, view
preferences, dismissed banners) must stub Storage first, or it is testing the
private-mode fallback rather than the feature. See
[[feedback-guards-must-assert-coverage]] and
[[feedback-mutation-test-new-tests]] — a mutation run is what exposes this,
since removing the persistence entirely still leaves the test green.

Done. **PR: https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto/pull/648** — one PR, 15 files, +1772/−482.

**Comparison page:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/28ab10d9-2359-41e1-805d-c3b5f39d562e

## On "why more PRs"

You were right about the split I proposed — I folded all four concerns into one branch. The concern is "make the Memory schema page usable," and legibility, panel authoring, the divider, and the redundant chip all serve it.

But there's one more PR I can't avoid, and it's structural, not a judgment call: **`packages/owletto` is its own repo** (`lobu-ai/owletto`), included as a submodule. So the code PR lands there, and the parent `lobu` repo then needs a separate PR that only moves the submodule pointer. Owletto merges first. That's two PRs for mechanical reasons, not scope reasons.

## The divider drags now

`role="separator"` between canvas and panel, doubling as the border. Verified against the prod backend:

| Gesture | Panel | Canvas |
|---|---|---|
| Rest | 288 | 799 |
| Drag left 150px | 438 | 649 |
| Reload | 438 | restored |
| Drag past window edge | 720 | 367 |
| Same, in a 1060px window | 387 | **320 exactly** |
| Double-click | 288 | override cleared |

A drag beats the mode default permanently — reverting to 440 when the editor opens would read as the handle being broken. Arrows nudge 16px, Home resets. Hand-rolled: no new dependency for `startWidth - dx` clamped.

## Two real bugs caught, one of them mine

`make review-fix` found that clamping against the flex **row** width overstates available space by the handle plus two gaps. I measured it live: row 1116 vs usable 1087, a 29px error that would have let the canvas drop below its promised floor. Now it measures `canvas.clientWidth + panel.clientWidth` — and the narrow-window test lands on exactly 320.

It also caught that in the **empty state** (zero types) my "Create entity type" button set a panel mode with no panel rendered — the same class of dead-click you found on mobile, in a branch I hadn't checked. Kept as a route there, since with no map to preserve the panel has no reason to exist.

I reviewed all five of its fixes against the source rather than taking the summary; the tap-to-reveal it added doesn't undo the legibility work — 2 count-pills at rest, names still off the canvas, now reachable by tap and screen reader instead of hover only.

## Verification

1128 tests pass, `tsc` clean, `make pre-pr` clean. I mutation-tested the new tests — flipped the drag direction, dropped the button guard, made the drag lose to the default, removed the canvas floor, unhid the handle on mobile. All five caught.

One correction worth flagging: my persistence tests were initially passing against nothing. jsdom 29 here has **no `localStorage` at all**, and `lib/storage.ts` swallows that into a null return — so the assertions were vacuous until I stubbed Storage. Saved to memory.

## Confidence

- **85 — resize, mobile, legibility.** Driven at real viewports against prod with DOM measurements; the clamp verified at the window size where it actually binds.
- **80 — the fixer's corrections.** Read the source and re-verified both live.
- **55 — save.** Unchanged and unproven. I never submitted a form; that writes to your real workspace and the edit target was Company with 2,035 records.

## Next actions

- Let me prove save with a throwaway type, then delete it — the last real gap, and I'd want your go-ahead since it writes to prod.
- Merge #648, then I'll open the parent-repo pointer PR (that worktree is behind `origin/main` and needs a pull first).
- Prod-verify after rollout, gated on the squash commit.
- Vite is still up on `localhost:5174` against the prod backend if you want to drag it yourself.

content.text:
Done — the `Memory` label drops to `text-sidebar-foreground/50` when the accordion is open, so it reads as the parent of the type rows rather than another one of them.

**One judgment call worth surfacing:** I made it recede *only when it isn't carrying the highlight*. Three states:

| State | Memory label |
|---|---|
| Collapsed | Full weight — no children to be confused with |
| Open, on `/memory` itself | Full weight, highlighted — being the current page outranks being a parent, and grey-on-accent reads as disabled |
| Open, browsing a type | **Greyed** — the confusing case |

That third row is the one you're describing: once you click into Person or Company, Memory loses its highlight and becomes pixel-identical to its own children. That's where it looked like an entity type.

Verified against prod at all three: greyed reads alpha `0.5` vs Company's full-strength accent; the other two stay at `0.8`.

Mutation-tested the three new tests — never recede, recede whenever open (ignoring the highlight), recede always (ignoring open). Each was caught.

**Two things worth noting:**

I hit the stale-browser-module trap again — my first live check showed the class missing even though vite was serving the edited source. Restarting vite fixed it; the code was always right. Third time this session that a stale dev-server cache has produced a false negative.

And my first DOM probe was wrong in a way that would have misled me: I checked `className.includes("bg-sidebar-accent")`, which also matches `hover:bg-sidebar-accent/60` — so every row looked highlighted. The existing tests in this file carry a comment warning about exactly that. Switched to `classList.contains`.

I left the type rows at the same indent as Memory. Re-indenting them would be the other way to carry hierarchy, but you asked for the grey and that's a bigger layout change than the ask.

This is on the same branch as PR #648 rather than a new one, since you'd rather not fan out PRs — but it isn't pushed yet, so say the word if you'd rather it stood alone.

## Confidence

**High (85)** — verified at all three states against prod with computed colors, plus mutation-tested tests. The full suite is still running in the background; I'll flag it if anything unrelated broke.

## Next actions

- Push the sidebar commit to #648 once the suite reports green, and update the comparison artifact with the sidebar before/after.
- The save path is still unproven — happy to test it with a throwaway type if you want.
- Merge #648, then the parent-repo submodule-pointer PR.

## What

The Memory schema map (`/$owner/memory`) was unreadable past a handful of types. Three defects visible in one screenshot: relationship labels collided into each other, long type names truncated to `Comp…`, and the unconnected-types column pushed the actual schema into a corner.

**Before / after screenshots + measurements:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/28ab10d9-2359-41e1-805d-c3b5f39d562e

## Legibility

- **Bundle by pair, not by relationship type.** Every relationship between the same two types shares one path — 6 paths become 3 on the reference workspace. A bundled path shows a count pill.
- **Names leave the resting canvas.** Disclosed on hover, on tap (edges are selectable and focusable), and through `aria-label`, so the disclosure is not mouse-only.
- **Boxes size themselves** from measured title and meta text, clamped 200–320px, with the name on its own line. It had shared a row with the counts and was the only flexible item on it, so identity always lost space to metadata.
- **`fitView` frames the connected subgraph**, so islands cannot push the schema off screen.

## Authoring moved into the panel

The relationship form was a modal covering the very boxes you pick between — its two inputs are From and To. Editing a type navigated away to `/$owner/entity-types/$slug`, hiding the map being edited. Both now render beside the canvas.

`EntityTypePage` is reused verbatim rather than reimplemented narrow; it gains a `compact` prop for the heading. The routed page stays — the entity-type rail still links to it.

## Resizable divider

The panel picks a width by mode (288 index / 440 editor); the divider drags to override that. Persisted, clamped so the canvas keeps a 320px floor, `Home`/double-click to reset. A ResizeObserver re-clamps on mount and on container resize, so a width saved on a wide display does not restore oversized on a narrow one. Hand-rolled — `react-resizable-panels` would bring a layout engine to a problem that is `startWidth - dx` clamped.

## Bugs fixed

**1. "Create entity type" was dead below `lg`.** The panel was `hidden lg:flex`, so the button set a mode nothing rendered.

- **Red:** at 390px, clicking it produced no editor; panel computed `display: none`.
- **Green:** panel `flex w-full`, name input 358px, canvas `offsetParent === null`, Cancel restores the canvas. Regression test: `keeps the divider off a narrow viewport, where there is no split`.

**2. The expanded Memory sidebar row read as one of its own children.** It shared the type rows' weight, size and indent; browsing a type moves the highlight off it, leaving it indistinguishable from the list below. Now recedes to `text-sidebar-foreground/50` while it has children on screen — but stays full weight when collapsed, and when the map itself is the open page.

**3. Duplicate form ids.** Both responsive presentations of the relationship form can be mounted with CSS choosing the visible one, so fixed ids bound each label to whichever copy mounted first. Now `useId`-scoped.

The empty state (zero types) still routes to the create page rather than the panel — with no map to keep visible the panel's reason does not apply, and no panel is rendered to receive the mode.

## Also

Drops the `Needs setup` filter chip from Connectors. The list already sorts needs-setup first and badges each card, so the chip restated what was on screen. Eight filters remain.

## Testing

- `bunx vitest run` — **1133 passed**, 128 files. `tsc --noEmit` clean. Parent `make pre-pr` clean.
- New tests mutation-tested: flipped the drag direction, dropped the primary-button guard, made the drag lose to the mode default, removed the canvas floor, unhid the handle below `lg`, and three variants of the sidebar rule. All caught.

### Save path exercised end-to-end against production

Driven through the real UI against `app.lobu.ai` on a throwaway type, then cleaned up:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Create type in the panel | Node appeared on the canvas live, no navigation |
| Rename it in the panel | Box updated in place; panel handed its width back |
| Add relationship (`Works At` → Company) | Edges 3 → 4, cluster 3 → 4 members |
| Remove the rule | Only the read-only catalog entry left |
| Delete the type | Back to 14 nodes / 3 edges |

**Caveat:** entity-type deletion is a *soft* delete by design ("can be restored by a database administrator"), so a tombstoned row for `zz-scratch-deleteme` remains in the workspace. Nothing else was written; `Company` and every existing type were never edited.

**owletto PR #648 is merged** (`df33325e`). The parent pointer PR is **lobu-ai/lobu#2365**, with `make review` running now — that posts the required `pi-review` status, so I'll merge once it reports.

## The save path is proven

You asked for it, so I ran it end to end against production on a throwaway type — never touching Company:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Create type in the panel | Node appeared on the canvas live, no navigation |
| Rename it | Box updated in place; panel handed its width back |

That was the last real gap. Confidence on save goes from 55 to **90**.

**One residue you should know about:** entity-type deletion is a *soft* delete by design — the UI says "can be restored by a database administrator". So a tombstoned `zz-scratch-deleteme` row remains in the workspace. The visible state is exactly as I found it, but I can't claim the write left zero trace.

## What review-fix caught this round

Two were real bugs in my code, not style:

**A restored width wasn't re-clamped.** I only clamped during a drag, so a 720px panel saved on a wide display would restore oversized on a laptop — and `aria-valuemax` advertised a ceiling the container couldn't honour. Now driven by a ResizeObserver on the split row.

**The relationship form used fixed element ids.** Both responsive presentations can be mounted at once with CSS choosing the visible one, so each label bound to whichever copy mounted first. Now `useId`-scoped — visible in the DOM as `_r_d_-relationship`.

It also deleted four payload fields as unused. I checked that structurally rather than taking its word: `fieldCount`/`entityCount` still compose `metaLabel`, and edge-level `isSymmetric` still suppresses the arrowhead — only the dead node-payload copies went.

It again asked me to split out the connector changes. I kept them, per your call.

## Two things I got wrong

I ran a broad `pkill -f vitest` and may have killed a test run belonging to another worktree — there are several dev servers from other sessions on this machine. Scoped to my own PIDs after that.

And a DOM probe using `className.includes("bg-sidebar-accent")` matched `hover:bg-sidebar-accent/60`, making every sidebar row look highlighted. The existing tests in that file carry a comment warning about exactly this. Switched to `classList.contains`.

## Final state

1133 tests, `tsc` clean, parent `make pre-pr` clean. 17 files, +1900/−540 across three commits.

- I'll merge #2365 as soon as `pi-review` reports.
- After rollout, prod-verify the map on `app.lobu.ai`, gated on the squash commit (not the branch head).
- Worth a follow-up: that rule-removal `x` button has no accessible name — pre-existing, and I left it alone.

git add -- src/components/entities/entity-type-graph-view.tsx src/components/entities/entity-type-graph-view.test.tsx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(owletto): reveal relationship names when an edge is reached by keyboard

Bundling the schema map's edges took relationship names off the resting
canvas and put them behind hover, a tap, and `aria-label`. Edges are tabbable,
so a keyboard user could reach one -- and nothing happened. Screen readers had
the names all along; sighted keyboard users had no way to get them.

React Flow fires neither `onEdgeClick` nor its own selection for a keypress on
a focused edge: measured in-browser, Enter and Space on a focused edge leave
the element unselected and emit no click. So nothing downstream of click or
selection could have carried this.

Focus is the keyboard's hover, so reveal on arrival rather than on a keypress.
React Flow owns the edge's `<g>` and exposes no prop on it, but it stamps the
edge id as `data-id`, and focus events reach the wrapper this component
already renders -- so the id is read on the way up instead of reaching into
the library.

Verified with real keystrokes against production: tabbing across three edges
reveals each one's names in turn and restores the counts on the ones left
behind; tabbing out to a button clears them.

Also corrects a test that claimed to cover keyboard users while only calling
`onEdgeClick` -- the very handler a keypress never reaches -- and teaches the
React Flow stub to render edges and nodes with the focusable, `data-id`
carrying shape the real library emits, so a focus test has something true to
run against.
EOF

Follow-up to #648, from a blocker its parent-repo review caught.

## The gap

#648 bundled the schema map's edges and moved relationship names off the resting canvas, behind hover, a tap, and `aria-label`. Edges are tabbable — so a keyboard user could reach one and **nothing happened**. Screen readers had the names via `aria-label` the whole time; sighted keyboard users had no way to get them.

## Why the obvious fix doesn't work

The review suggested syncing from React Flow's selection. Measured in-browser on the merged build, that would not have worked:

```
focus an edge   -> tabindex="0", document.activeElement === the edge   OK
press Enter     -> chips stay ["3","2"]      no reveal
press Space     -> chips stay ["3","2"]      no reveal
edge classList  -> "selectable" but NOT "selected"
```

React Flow fires neither `onEdgeClick` nor its own selection for a keypress on a focused edge. Nothing downstream of click or selection could carry this.

## The fix

Focus is the keyboard's hover, so reveal on arrival rather than on a keypress. React Flow owns the edge's `<g>` and exposes no prop on it, but it stamps the edge id as `data-id`, and focus events reach the wrapper this component already renders — so the id is read on the way up rather than reaching into the library.

`onBlurCapture` clears unconditionally: `focusout` on the element being left always precedes `focusin` on the one being entered, which I measured rather than assumed (`focusin:A → focusout:A → focusin:B`).

## Verified with real keystrokes against production

| Action | Focused | Canvas |
|---|---|---|
| Focus edge 1 | `pair:$member\|company` | `["Claims Identity Has Authority Proposes Merge With", "2"]` |
| Tab | `pair:$member\|$member` | `["3", "Claims Identity Proposes Merge With"]` |
| Tab | `pair:person\|company` | `["3", "2", "Works At"]` |
| Tab | a button | `["3", "2"]` — cleared |

Exactly one edge revealed at a time, following focus, restored on leaving.

## Tests

**Also fixes a test that lied.** #648 carried `lets touch and keyboard users reveal relationship names from an edge`, which only called `onEdgeClick` — the handler a keypress never reaches. It asserted nothing about keyboard users and would have passed with the bug present. Renamed to what it actually covers, and a real keyboard test added that drives focus through the rendered element.

That required teaching the React Flow stub to render edges and nodes with the focusable, `data-id`-carrying shape the real library emits — otherwise there is nothing true to focus.

Mutation-tested: dropping `focusedEdgeId` from the reveal predicate, removing the focus wiring, and removing the blur wiring are each caught. 1136 tests pass, `tsc` clean.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
I merged #648 before running the parent-repo review, and that review caught a real accessibility blocker. Fixing it forward as **owletto#650**, waiting on CI.

## The blocker was real, and mine

Bundling the edges took relationship names off the resting canvas. Edges are tabbable, so a keyboard user could reach one and **nothing happened**. Screen readers had the names via `aria-label` all along; sighted keyboard users had no path to them.

I reproduced it before touching code:

```
focus edge   → activeElement === the edge, tabindex="0"   ✓
press Enter  → chips stay ["3","2"]                       ✗
press Space  → chips stay ["3","2"]                       ✗
```

**The reviewer's suggested fix would not have worked.** It proposed syncing from React Flow's `onSelectionChange` — but the edge's classList after Enter reads `selectable` and *not* `selected`. React Flow never selects it, so nothing downstream of selection could carry this. Verifying the claim before acting on it is what surfaced that.

The fix reveals on **focus** instead — focus is the keyboard's hover. React Flow owns the edge `<g>` and exposes no prop on it, but stamps `data-id`, and focus events reach the wrapper I already render.

Verified with real Tab keystrokes against prod: three edges, each revealing its own names in turn, counts restored behind, cleared on tabbing out to a button.

## Two things my own tests got wrong

**A test that lied.** #648 shipped `lets touch and keyboard users reveal relationship names from an edge` — which only called `onEdgeClick`, the handler a keypress never reaches. It would have passed with the bug present. That's how this escaped. Renamed to what it covers, and a real keyboard test added that drives focus through the rendered element. That meant teaching the React Flow stub to emit the focusable, `data-id`-carrying shape the real library does.

**Two guards I wrote were speculative, and my comments overstated them.** Mutation testing showed a blur-ordering guard and a scoping check that no test could kill. Rather than write tests to justify them, I checked the actual behavior: `focusout:A` fires *before* `focusin:B`, so the guard was unnecessary — I'd had the ordering backwards in a code comment. Deleted it, simplified to an unconditional clear, and rewrote the scoping comment to say what's true (it states intent; node ids can't collide with `pair:` edge ids) rather than claim a bug it doesn't prevent.

1136 tests, `tsc` clean, three of four mutations caught — the survivor is a genuine no-op equivalence, not a gap.

## State

- **owletto#648** — merged (`df33325e`)
- **owletto#650** — open, keyboard fix, waiting on CodeRabbit
- **lobu#2365** — parent pointer, open, still points at `df33325e`. I'm holding it; once #650 merges I'll repoint and re-run `make review`.

## Confidence

**High (85)** on the keyboard fix — reproduced the bug, verified the fix with real keystrokes, mutation-tested.

**Lower on my process here (60).** I merged the submodule before the parent review ran, which is what let a blocker land on `main`. The right order is parent review first, then merge owletto — worth correcting for next time.

## Next

- Merge #650 when CI reports, repoint #2365, re-run `make review`, merge.
- Then prod-verify after rollout, gated on the squash commit.

## Blocker 1 — real, fixed in owletto#652

`apps/mac/Owletto/LobuClient.swift`, from #647 (someone else's Mac work). `decodeIfPresent(String.self, …)` returns nil only for a *missing* key — on a JSON number it **throws**, so the `else if` Int fallback was unreachable and a numeric `behavior_id` failed the entire Behaviors response. ## Blocker 2 — false positive, not fixing

The claim was that the Mac resume loop can never fire because the gateway has no matching contract. But that contract is in **PR #2361**, unmerged — I grepped its diff and found exactly the `status: "resume"` / `completeWindow not called — resume allowed` handling it says is missing. The reviewer read the submodule range in isolation, without its server counterpart.

That split is the repo's own owletto-first rule. If my pointer lands before #2361, the loop stays inert — today's behavior — not broken. I'm not touching another session's in-flight feature to satisfy a finding that context explains.

This is the second time this session a reviewer's suggested fix was wrong on the facts (the earlier one proposed syncing React Flow selection that never happens). Verifying before acting is what caught both.

## Why this keeps happening

Submodule pointer bumps are transitive: my one-line PR carries five owletto merges from several sessions, so `make review` audits all of them and hands me other people's blockers. That's the mechanism, not bad luck.

  directions permanently. Reverting to the mode default when the editor opens
  reads as the handle being broken.
- Resize is hand-rolled — `react-resizable-panels` is not a dep and would bring
  a layout engine to `startWidth - dx` clamped.
- Clamp against `canvas.clientWidth + panel.clientWidth`, NOT the flex row:
  the row overstates by the handle + gaps (29px measured) and lets the canvas
  fall under its 320px floor. Re-clamp on mount + ResizeObserver, not only
  mid-drag, or a width saved on a wide display restores oversized.

  AND unhighlighted. Grey-on-accent reads as disabled.

Mid-task the shell cwd reset to `~/Code/lobu` and my `cd packages/owletto` landed in the **main checkout** instead of the worktree. I ran `git checkout main`, `git reset --hard origin/main`, and created a branch there — a direct violation of "never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly."

The trap is that `cd` inside a compound command doesn't persist the way I assumed across tool calls. I'm using absolute paths and checking `pwd` from here.

Each review round surfaces the next one because a pointer bump is transitive: my one-line PR audits five other merges.

`LocalAgentDetector.searchPrefixes()` searches `$PATH` plus `~/.bun/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`. Its own comment states why:

Route both through the detector's own list instead of adding a fourth copy. There were already three: the detector's, the child-process `PATH` the dispatcher injects, and `locateOnPath`'s. - **Running many `make review` in parallel exhausts the shared Codex GPT-5.5 quota** → HTTP 429 `usage_limit_reached`, credits balance 0, **primary window resets in ~4-5h** (300-min window). ~5 concurrent review sessions burned it for the rest of the day. **Serialize reviews** (one at a time), or you block every PR's verdict for hours. Check reset via the `X-Codex-Primary-Reset-At` epoch in the 429 body.

## What

The device-held finalize loop in `WatcherDispatcher.dispatch` decides durable delivery state for a Behavior run, and had no direct coverage — only the helpers around it did. This adds `DispatcherResumeTests`, and deletes three declarations with no reader.

## Why this loop

It is where the expensive mistakes live: re-spawning the CLI when the server only wanted the report re-sent, burning a fresh finalize attempt on a retry, or answering an ambiguous delivery with a failure report that contradicts a decision the server already committed.

## No production change was needed

Both seams already existed: `LocalAgentExecutor` is a protocol, and `WorkerClient.init` takes an injectable `URLSession`. The test drives the **real** `WorkerClient` over a stubbed transport, so assertions are on the wire body the server would actually receive — not on a mock's recollection of it.

## Covered

| | |
|---|---|
| granted resume | re-spawns with the server's nudge, reports the server's `attempt` |
| transient delivery failure | re-sends the same `finalize_attempt`, does **not** re-run the CLI |
| non-retriable failure | posts nothing further |
| unreadable 2xx body | neither a completion nor a resume |
| server stuck on resume | local cap bounds it at 8 spawns, then an explicit error |

The resume fixture scripts `attempt: 2`, not `1` — after one resume a local `+ 1` also yields `1`, so a `1` would pass whether or not the server's count is honoured.

Each mutation flips the suite red; baseline and restore pass.

## A doc error the tests found

An unreadable 2xx body does **not** reach `completeWithError`, as the comments claimed. It is classified as a non-retriable delivery failure and left for the server's heartbeat-stale sweep. Verified against `origin/main` (not the working tree) that each has no reader anywhere in the repo: `DevicePermissionKind.shortLabel`, the `notificationsStatusLoaded` dead write, and `enum DevicePermissionsSnapshot`.

## What

One-line submodule pointer bump, `a23fe0d1` → `3fab87fa`. Carries exactly one owletto PR: [owletto#657](https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto/pull/657).

## Why

The device-held finalize loop in `WatcherDispatcher.dispatch` decides durable delivery state for a Behavior run and had no direct coverage — only the helpers around it did. This is the coverage gap `pi-review` flagged on #2365.

`DispatcherResumeTests` drives the **real** `WatcherDispatcher` through a stubbed `URLSession` and a recording executor, so assertions are on the wire body the server would actually receive. No production change was needed to make it testable: `LocalAgentExecutor` was already a protocol and `WorkerClient.init` already took an injectable `URLSession`.

Covered: a granted resume re-spawns with the server's nudge and reports the server's `attempt`; a transient delivery failure re-sends the same `finalize_attempt` without re-running the CLI; a non-retriable failure posts nothing further; an unreadable 2xx body is neither a completion nor a resume; and the local safety cap bounds the loop at 8 spawns.

The gate wanted dispatcher-level tests. My earlier claim that I'd have to invent #2361's contract was **wrong** — asserting *what the Mac sends* needs no server semantics, and both seams already existed (`LocalAgentExecutor` is a protocol, `WorkerClient.init` takes an injectable `URLSession`). Zero production changes needed.

if !retriable { return nil }              -> (removed)  killed
localMaxRounds = 8                        -> 16         killed
