```

The tests caught a doc error too: an unreadable 2xx body doesn't reach `completeWithError` as the comments claimed — it's a non-retriable delivery failure left to the sweep. Fixed in both places. Also deleted the three dead `DevicePermissions` declarations.

## But I hit a real bug and stopped

My pointer PR **#2368** got a new blocker, and this time **the reviewer is right**. owletto#656 landed while I worked — it stops telling event turns to call `completeWindow`. The server half doesn't exist: `run-lifecycle.ts` fails every clean still-running exit, and `trigger_execution` appears nowhere in `worker-api/`. **Every device event turn would be marked failed.**

Prod is safe — main's pointer `a23fe0d1` predates #656. It ships the moment any pointer bump lands.

That's why **#2366, #2367, and #2368 are all BLOCKED on the same thing**. #2366/#2367 are byte-identical, opened 30s apart — another of your sessions hit this wall and stopped too. Mine supersedes both.

I stopped rather than build it. It's the missing half of a feature — durable run state, completion event, `last_fired_at`, plus an integration test — in a lane another session is active in. Two sessions independently implementing the same contract is the worst outcome. I've localized it precisely: `approved.trigger_execution === "turn"` is already in scope at `run-lifecycle.ts:793`, no new query needed.

- **Schema map shipped: 95** — health revision + CSS markers, both fetched.
- **Panel *works* in prod: 60** — code is served; I never drove it. Chrome extension is disconnected.

**RESOLVED 2026-07-30.** Both halves are on main.

owletto#656 (`f8097963`) stopped telling event turns to call `completeWindow` —
the reply IS the work. For a few hours the server had no matching branch, so
`run-lifecycle.ts` would have failed every clean device event-turn exit.
**lobu#2361** (`a23ad740f`) landed the server half at exactly the right
predicate — `approved.trigger_execution === "turn"` → `finalizeRun(status:
"completed", window_id = NULL)` — and bumped the pointer in the same PR. It
never reached prod broken.

## The durable lesson: a pointer bump is not "one line"

A one-line submodule bump carries **every** owletto commit in the range,
including other people's unshipped features. `pi-review` audits all of it and
will hand back blockers for code you did not write. Twice in one day my
"trivial" pointer PR was blocked by another lane's work.

The fix is to make the range small: bump onto **current** main so the
transitive range is only your own commits. Rebasing #2368 onto main took its
verdict from `bug_free 15, 1 blocker` to `bug_free 88, 0 blockers,
tests_adequate: true` — same content, smaller range.

Corollary: **a stale pointer PR becomes a revert.** #2366/#2367 targeted
`f8097963`; once main moved to `3fab87fa`, merging either would have walked the
pointer backward and dropped owletto#657. Closed them. Always check
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <PR-target> <main-pointer>` before merging a
pointer bump — see [[feedback-stale-tree-commit-reverts-merged-work]].

## Reviewer was RIGHT here
Contrast [[project-schema-map-legibility-and-panel]], where two suggested fixes
were wrong. Judge by the finding, not the score: this verdict's `bug_free 15`
came with an env blocker (`mktemp` EPERM, CI queued) yet the blocker was real
and precisely localized to file+line+predicate. Verify each finding on its own
merits — neither trust nor dismiss by score.
See [[feedback-judge-reviews-by-findings-not-scores]].

## Concurrent sessions share branches
Another session pushed a merge to `pointer-657` while I was merging main into
it locally. Both resolutions were byte-identical, so I reset to theirs rather
than push a divergent merge. `git fetch` + compare trees before force-anything;
never force-push a branch another session may hold.
See [[feedback-concurrent-agent-worktree-wipe]].

# Done — everything's merged

The thing that unblocked it: **#2361 landed while we talked**, shipping the event-turn server half at exactly the predicate I'd identified. The blocker I stopped on evaporated, and rebasing onto current main shrank my PR's transitive range to just my own commit.

That alone moved the verdict, same content:

```

**#2368 merged** as `9f0c3e16`. Main's owletto pointer is `3fab87fa`, and all the work is verified present there — `schema-panel-resize.ts`, its tests, `DispatcherResumeTests.swift`, `focusedEdgeId` (3 refs), `needs_setup` gone.

## Also cleaned up

I closed **#2366 and #2367**. They weren't just redundant — they'd become *reverts*. Both set the pointer to `f8097963`, and main is now at the descendant `3fab87fa`, so merging either would have walked the pointer backward and dropped the dispatcher tests. Verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before closing, and the closing comment explains why so nobody reopens them blindly.

Only unrelated PRs remain open (voice profiles, min_scrolls, the release).

## What's actually left: one thing

**The interactive verify.** The schema map is confirmed *shipped* — prod serves `--schema-panel-width`, `schema-panel`, `cursor-col-resize` in its CSS — but that proves the code is there, not that the handle drags or that the keyboard reveal fires. I couldn't check that because the Chrome extension is disconnected.

Reconnect it and I'll do it in a couple of minutes. That's the only open item.

Nothing else is owed. #2368 has no prod-visible surface (Swift tests + dead-code deletion), so it needs no rollout gate.

## Two things I'd flag

**A pointer bump is never "one line."** It carries every commit in the range, and `pi-review` audits all of it — twice today my trivial bump was blocked by another lane's code. Bumping onto *current* main is what fixes it.

**Another session was pushing to my branch.** It merged main into `pointer-657` while I did the same locally. The resolutions were byte-identical so I took theirs, but that's a real collision risk worth knowing about if you're running sessions in parallel. Both lessons are in memory.
